Action Plan:
1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI): Continue paracetamol as needed; may add Day Nurse / Night Nurse (compatible with metformin & lisinopril). Encourage hydration, rest, and symptomatic care. Safety-net: seek medical review if shortness of breath, wheeze, fever develops, or if symptoms persist > 3 weeks or worsen.
2. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). Maintain regular home glucose monitoring; keep good hydration while unwell; consult if readings become abnormal.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented). Continue home BP checks; no adjustment required today.
4. Follow-up: Patient to arrange GP review if red-flag symptoms occur or if any chronic condition becomes uncontrolled.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 5-day history of cough and “cold” symptoms.  
• History of presenting illness: Dry, hacking cough; runny nose; myalgias; occasional headache; chills. No sputum, hemoptysis, shortness of breath, wheeze, or chest tightness.  
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes (~5–6 years); mild hypertension.  
• Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril; Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented). No ibuprofen used.  
• Allergies: Not elicited.  
• Social history: Patient in secure location; smoking/alcohol not discussed.

Objective:
• Video inspection of oropharynx: Mild pharyngeal erythema; tonsils not enlarged; no exudate.  
• Neck: No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy (patient-reported).  
• Vitals: Home BP today “within normal range” (exact values not provided). No other vitals recorded.  
• Chest not examined; patient denies respiratory distress.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Cough / Cold symptoms  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold). Supported by DDx item “Viral URTI – High likelihood.”  
   - Differential diagnosis: • Influenza / influenza-like illness (DDx Medium); • ACE-inhibitor–induced cough (DDx Low-Medium); • Allergic rhinitis / post-nasal drip (DDx Low).  
   - Investigations: None indicated at this time.  
   - Treatment: Symptomatic care—paracetamol; optional Day Nurse / Night Nurse. Encourage fluids, rest.  
   - Referrals: None.

2. Diabetes mellitus type 2 (stable)  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Known diabetes, currently well controlled (patient-reported).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.  
   - Investigations: None today.  
   - Treatment: Continue metformin; maintain glucose monitoring.  
   - Referrals: None.

3. Hypertension (stable)  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Essential hypertension, controlled on lisinopril.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.  
   - Investigations: None today.  
   - Treatment: Continue lisinopril; continue home BP monitoring.  
   - Referrals: None.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies, smoking/alcohol status, current medication doses, full vitals (HR, RR, SpO₂, temperature), vaccination status.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, minor conversational fillers; clinically adequate information captured.
